profile.reading: This H5 Data Centers facility is located at 21800 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147, in the Northern Virginia data center corridor. The operator own facility page describes a 255,000 square foot new build with access to 42 MW from Dominion Power and up to 60 MVA available, built to a Tier III, N plus 2C design. The page states a targeted LEED Silver certification along with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance. H5 Data Centers is a privately held US colocation and wholesale data center operator with facilities spanning roughly two dozen markets nationwide, per the company's own site, of which this Ashburn facility is one of its largest publicized builds. This address sits within Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley," the single densest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside campuses operated by NTT, Digital Realty, Aligned, and numerous other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry; H5's own page cites access to up to 60 MVA from Dominion Energy as a selling point specific to this build, well above the smaller facilities the company operates in secondary markets like Portland or San Antonio. H5 is not a publicly traded company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's power, cooling, and certification details are sourced solely to the operator's own published facility page rather than an independently corroborating source, a limitation this registry notes rather than treats as disqualifying, consistent with its general practice for privately held colocation operators. No year-opened date or third-party audited capacity figure was located for this specific address this session. The 42 MW power figure cited by the operator reflects utility access rather than a certified critical-IT-load rating, a distinction this entry preserves rather than treats as equivalent.

reading.body:
H5's Ashburn facility can draw 42 MW from Dominion Power, making it a mid-scale node in Northern Virginia's data center corridor but below the gigawatt-scale builds now required for training frontier models.

The 255,000 square foot building sits in Ashburn, where power density and grid access have long made the region attractive for hyperscaler infrastructure. The 42 MW capacity reflects the scale of workload many enterprises can absorb, particularly for inference and smaller training jobs. The facility's Tier III design with N plus 2C redundancy signals the operator's focus on availability rather than the cutting-edge reliability now standard in newer builds.

For AI specifically, this facility's power constraint matters more than its square footage. Forty-two megawatts supports perhaps a few thousand GPUs at typical utilization, which is sufficient for deployed models but represents a fraction of the compute needed to train or fine-tune large language models. The lack of published total capacity figures, only power access, underscores how power now binds facility utility in ways square footage alone no longer does.

The data does not cover actual current utilization, tenant mix, cooling architecture, or whether Dominion can sustain 42 MW at peak demand across Northern Virginia's growing data center load. The targeted LEED Silver rating suggests environmental compliance priorities that impose their own cost and operational constraints.
